target_source: checkpoint-32 Raspberry Pi transcripts, failure bundle, and support bundle supplied by operator

observed.detail: Commit 636285827c8947ba689400c9b1dc217ea5521130 built and activated, passed runtime/I2C/model/speech/application-service prerequisites, then stopped because preferred Bluetooth AIRHUG was paired but did not connect.
Subsequent remote curl and local-checkpoint runs of the same commit stopped at immutable_release with RELEASE_ACTIVE_INVALID / RELEASE_INVALID.
Support snapshot exposes AIRHUG USB capture and playback devices; deterministic direct USB duplex audio therefore exists independently of Bluetooth connection state.
Target transcript shows /dev/i2c-1 and SHT31 at 0x44.
Support service events counted WAKE_LED_GPIO_LINE_AMBIGUOUS repeatedly while the target snapshot identifies GPIO17/GPIO22/GPIO23/GPIO27 on the Raspberry Pi 5 header controller.
Prior target evidence preserved GPIO23 manual 0/OFF, 1/ON, 0/OFF physical fan response.

root_causes.detail: Privileged post-seal Python CLI execution can create __pycache__/pyc inside the current immutable release. Checkpoint 32 treated those derived runtime artifacts as authoritative payload drift, creating a same-commit rerun dead-end.
The pairing step treated requested Bluetooth connection as mandatory even when deterministic direct USB capture/playback was available.
Interaction GPIO resolvers failed on duplicate GPIO<n> names across gpiochips rather than preferring the unique Pi-5 RP1 header-controller match.
